title: A tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess

concept.text: The innovation would be a quantitatively tested explanation of how the early universe acquired its surviving excess of baryons over antibaryons. Baryons constitute ordinary matter, and their present abundance is measured, while the present-day density of antibaryons is negligible. The unresolved task is to identify the physical process that produced this imbalance and connect its predicted outcome to observations.

A successful mechanism would connect microscopic interactions and an explicit early-universe history to the measured baryon abundance. Electroweak baryogenesis is one candidate: it requires new physics that makes the electroweak transition sufficiently strongly first order, together with additional violation of CP symmetry—the symmetry relating particles and antiparticles with spatial directions reversed. Leptogenesis is another candidate identified in the supplied review. Neither is established as the origin of the observed excess.

Proposed definition of completion: the achievement would combine a successful abundance prediction from independently constrained inputs with an observed, quantitatively connected signature of the same scenario. This definition demands an explanation that survives independent testing; it is a proposed evidential goal, not an established consensus standard or a claim that every conceivable mechanism must have an accessible signature.

significance.text: Identifying the responsible process would explain why the observed net baryon excess survives and connect a cosmological abundance to microscopic physics. Within the standard hot-big-bang framework discussed in the review, Standard Model CP violation and out-of-equilibrium dynamics are insufficient for successful baryogenesis. A tested explanation would therefore identify the additional physics responsible for a basic feature of the observable universe. Its explanatory scope is the surviving excess, rather than the broader question of why matter or the universe exists at all.

The direct scientific consequence would be a predictive connection between early-universe evolution and independently tested interactions. For electroweak scenarios, the review identifies possible connections to Higgs-sector physics, collider measurements, electric dipole moments and gravitational waves. Which measurements could reveal the mechanism depends on the particular scenario; these probe classes do not guarantee an observable signal in every viable model.

Conditional synthesis: once established, such a connection could guide further experiments and constrain alternative accounts of the early universe. Under the proposed completion criterion, an independently observed signature would be part of the achievement itself. No particular technology, method of manufacturing antimatter or change to the universe’s ultimate fate follows directly from explaining the baryon excess.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a tested dynamical account of baryon production, including the conditions under which it occurred. In the conventional CPT-invariant framework, the relevant ingredients are baryon-number violation, violation of C and CP symmetries, and departure from thermal equilibrium. C symmetry exchanges particles with antiparticles. The equilibrium requirement needs its stated qualification: the review explicitly notes that an asymmetry can arise without departure from thermal equilibrium if CPT is violated. These conventional ingredients describe requirements for a class of explanations; identifying them does not identify the actual cosmic mechanism.

For electroweak baryogenesis, the scientific barriers include establishing a sufficiently strong first-order electroweak transition, identifying adequate additional CP violation, and showing that the resulting dynamics generate the observed abundance while satisfying experimental constraints. Collider and electric-dipole-moment searches increasingly restrict candidate scenarios. The challenge is therefore to find a quantitatively successful, experimentally allowed mechanism, rather than merely to propose interactions capable of producing an asymmetry in principle.

Reliable prediction is itself unfinished work. The review describes large theoretical uncertainties in calculated baryon yields, with their sizes not always well understood, and emphasizes precise predictions for both abundance and corresponding experimental signatures in specific scenarios. Closing this gap requires controlled calculations with explicit assumptions and uncertainties. Experimentally, a candidate signal would also need a sufficiently quantitative connection to the proposed cosmic history to distinguish the mechanism from other explanations of that signal.

current_state.text: The abundance target is measured. The Planck 2018 cosmological-parameters analysis, published in 2020, reports Ω_b h² = 0.0224 ± 0.0001 in its base-ΛCDM abstract, with uncertainties stated at 68% confidence. Here Ω_b is the baryon density relative to the critical density and h is the dimensionless Hubble parameter. The more precise baseline result retained in the supplied review is Ω_b h² = 0.02237 ± 0.00015 at 68% confidence for Planck TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing. These are differently presented results from the same analysis, not conflicting measurements. Their interpretation retains the stated cosmological-model and data-combination scope. No independently sourced numerical baryon-to-photon ratio is supplied here.

The mechanism remains unresolved in the dated evidence supplied. Jorinde van de Vis, Jordy de Vries and Marieke Postma’s “Bubble Trouble: a Review on Electroweak Baryogenesis” was submitted on 13 August 2025, revised on 15 July 2026 and published in Progress in Particle and Nuclear Physics in 2026. It describes the origin of the asymmetry as an open problem, electroweak baryogenesis as increasingly constrained by experiments, and precise scenario-specific predictions as unfinished work. Collider, electric-dipole-moment and gravitational-wave measurements are discussed as probes of aspects of these scenarios, rather than as existing confirmation of a baryogenesis mechanism.

The review’s unresolved-origin assessment is consistent with there being no confirmed mechanism, but it is not an exhaustive audit against the abundance-plus-independent-signature criterion proposed here. The supplied freshness search record is empty, so the materials establish a July 2026 assessment rather than comprehensive coverage through 1 November 2026.

The supplied evidence review relied on intact passages within partial document extractions. Both PDF extractions were truncated, and the electroweak-review extraction ended during section 3.4.1. The Planck extraction additionally reported skipped form content. These limitations restrict conclusions about material outside the retained passages, but do not obscure the quoted abundance results or the review’s documented discussion of the unresolved origin and theoretical uncertainties. They do not establish that omitted results are false or absent.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: publish one specified mechanism with its microscopic inputs, cosmological history, calculation methods and theoretical uncertainties, and show that independently constrained quantities predict the measured baryon abundance. Agreement should be assessed against both observational and theoretical uncertainty. Adjusting otherwise unconstrained parameters solely to reproduce the abundance would not, by itself, meet this proposed criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed independent test: observe a signature that the same specified scenario quantitatively requires, and demonstrate that the combined abundance and signature evidence discriminates against plausible alternatives. The review grounds electric dipole moments, collider evidence connected to electroweak-transition physics and gravitational-wave spectra from that transition as possible probe classes. An observation in one of these classes would need an established connection to the abundance calculation; its existence alone would not identify the cosmic mechanism. These are scenario-dependent opportunities, not universally available tests.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed independent test

completion_criteria.text: Proposed extension: a measured lepton-number-violating rate could contribute to an analogous demonstration if a specified scenario quantitatively connects that rate, its cosmological history and the resulting baryon abundance. The retained excerpts do not establish such a relationship, so this remains a possible test to develop rather than a documented route to confirmation. Likewise, a proton-decay observation without a quantitative connection to the asymmetry, or a more precise abundance measurement alone, would not satisfy the proposed combined test.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed extension

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary checks: independent groups should be able to reproduce the abundance and signature predictions from disclosed inputs and methods, while independent observations test the relevant signatures. The analysis should state its sensitivity to cosmological assumptions, remaining unconstrained parameters and competing interpretations. Such finite demonstrations would establish support within the tested scenario and parameter range; they would not prove literal uniqueness among all conceivable mechanisms or universality across untested cosmic histories.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and boundary checks

related_concepts.text: Conceptual comparison with PHY-07, “Observation of baryon-number violation”: baryon-number violation is one of the conventional ingredients discussed for baryogenesis. PHY-07 concerns observing that physical phenomenon; PHY-13 concerns establishing its role within a quantitatively tested history of the cosmic excess. Proton decay is a possible model-dependent connection mentioned in the research, but the retained excerpts do not establish a particular proton-decay channel, rate or necessary relationship to the successful cosmological mechanism. The two objectives therefore remain distinct.

Conceptual comparison with PHY-08, “Observation of lepton-number violation”: the review identifies leptogenesis as an alternative candidate for explaining the asymmetry. This provides a prospective connection to lepton-number physics, but PHY-08 and PHY-13 ask different questions: observing a symmetry-violating process and explaining a cosmic abundance. Neutrinoless double beta decay is a possible model-dependent overlap named in the research. The supplied retained evidence does not determine how either an observation or a null search would constrain the relevant leptogenesis scenarios.

Conceptual comparison with PHY-12, “Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale”: electroweak baryogenesis can involve new Higgs-sector physics, creating potential overlap in particles, interactions and collider probes. Establishing a suitable electroweak transition and CP violation would address the origin of the baryon excess; explaining what sets the Higgs-mass scale is a separate objective. The supplied evidence does not establish that the same new physics would solve both problems.

change_log.change: Preserved PHY-13 and its title while defining the achievement as a quantitatively tested dynamical explanation of the surviving baryon excess.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent despite limitations in some supporting assertions, and the innovation has not been achieved in the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Replaced the broad explanation of why ordinary matter exists with the narrower explanation of the observed surviving net baryon excess.
change_log.reason: Baryogenesis addresses the asymmetry, not the ultimate existence of matter.

change_log.change: Added C violation and qualified the conventional departure-from-equilibrium requirement with CPT invariance.
change_log.reason: The retained review explicitly identifies these distinctions and notes the CPT-violating exception.

change_log.change: Retained the Planck abstract value alongside the more precise baseline result, including confidence level, data combination and base-ΛCDM scope.
change_log.reason: This preserves the supported quantitative detail without treating differently presented values as contradictory or inventing a baryon-to-photon ratio.

change_log.change: Integrated electroweak-transition requirements, experimental constraints and substantial baryon-yield uncertainties into the explanation of the missing breakthrough.
change_log.reason: These details explain why a plausible mechanism is insufficient without controlled predictions and independent tests.

change_log.change: Dated the unresolved-origin assessment to the review revised in July 2026 and preserved document-extraction and freshness limitations.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish exhaustive November 2026 coverage or full-document inspection.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion criterion to include cosmological assumptions, theoretical uncertainties, independent reproduction and discrimination against alternatives.
change_log.reason: An abundance fit or isolated signal would not establish the claimed causal explanation.

change_log.change: Preserved the lepton-number-violating-rate test as an explicitly unsupported proposal rather than silently deleting it.
change_log.reason: The research contains a potentially useful extension, but the retained evidence does not establish its quantitative connection to baryogenesis.

change_log.change: Used the roster’s broader identities for PHY-07 and PHY-08 and retained proton decay and neutrinoless double beta decay as qualified examples; added the documented Higgs-sector connection to PHY-12.
change_log.reason: Related concepts should remain distinct, and model-dependent connections should not be presented as demonstrated causal relationships.

unresolved_issues: Comprehensive developments after the July 2026 review revision and through 1 November 2026 are not established by the supplied materials.
The actual baryogenesis mechanism remains unidentified; the evidence does not select electroweak baryogenesis, leptogenesis or another scenario.
The retained evidence does not quantify how proton decay or neutrinoless double beta decay would constrain a specified successful mechanism, including the implications of null double-beta searches.
The proposed lepton-number-violating-rate test needs a concrete scenario and a supported quantitative connection to the baryon abundance.
The abundance-plus-independent-signature criterion is a proposed evidential goal. Its practical feasibility and ability to distinguish alternatives must be assessed for each scenario.
Truncated PDF extractions, including skipped Planck form content, leave material outside the retained passages unassessed.
